name: Heroku Platform MCP
description: Self-hosted Heroku Platform MCP server. Multi-user, OAuth-protected, deployable in one click.

HEROKUMCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID.description: Don't have one yet? Open a terminal and run:    heroku clients:create 'My Heroku MCP' 'https://YOUR-APP-NAME.herokuapp.com/oauth/callback'    -- replacing YOUR-APP-NAME with the App name you'll pick above. The command prints a client_id and client_secret. Paste the client_id here. Looks like a UUID, e.g. cf136ec2-3d0f-4f6c-916d-2e1f8501cd4e.

HEROKUMCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET.description: The client_secret printed by the same heroku clients:create command above. Treat this like a password -- it is encrypted at rest by the server.

HEROKUMCP_ADMIN_CONTACT.description: Email address for the initial admin user. Sign-ins from this email will be allowed; all others will be denied until you add them to MCP_ALLOWED_EMAILS or MCP_ALLOWED_TEAMS after deploy.

HEROKUMCP_MASTER_KEY.description: Auto-generated 32-byte secret for encrypting stored Heroku tokens at rest. Do not change this after deploy -- losing or rotating it invalidates every stored token (users will have to re-sign-in).

HEROKUMCP_OAUTH_SCOPE.description: OAuth scope the MCP requests. Leave as-is for least-privilege: full platform tools, no usage/billing. Type `global` to grant elevated access. Enabling this does NOT by itself let you see usage and billing -- your Heroku user must also have billing/enterprise-admin permission; if it does not, the MCP will fail when it attempts those calls. Typing `global` confirms you want to grant the MCP these elevated permissions. (Use the single word `global`, not `identity,global`.)

HEROKUMCP_PUBLIC_URL.description: Public URL of this deployed server. Leave blank -- the postdeploy script will set it automatically to https://<app-name>.herokuapp.com.

SOURCE_TAG.description: Git tag of StratisLLC/heroku-platform-mcp-server to deploy. Bump this when a new version ships.
